name: sol_basics_payment_4
description: Missing minimum deposit/withdrawal threshold enabling dust-amount rounding or DoS exploits
question: The source file in `source` implements a deposit or withdrawal function that accepts any nonzero amount without enforcing a minimum threshold, allowing dust-sized amounts to be processed such that share/asset conversion rounding or repeated tiny operations can corrupt accounting balances or be exploited for denial-of-service, excluding functions that already enforce a minimum amount check or revert on zero/negligible amounts, and excluding admin-only or trusted-role restricted functions.
criteria: deposit(uint256 amount) transfers tokens and mints shares via a division-based conversion formula without checking amount against any minimum value
withdraw(uint256 amount) burns shares and transfers underlying assets computed by rounding division with no floor/minimum enforced, letting dust withdrawals zero out shares while assets remain
a public deposit function only checks amount > 0 but allows amounts small enough that share calculation rounds down to zero shares minted
a loop or accounting structure updates per-user balances on every deposit call regardless of size, enabling unbounded dust deposits that inflate storage or gas costs for later processing
